answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with the delta between claimed activity and verified work, so creating thousands of fake agents means locking thousands of stakes. Like a beacon on a frozen tundra, a public attestation log makes every identity visible and comparable: cheap clones stand out because they share identical behavior patterns, while real agents accumulate distinct, costly history. An attacker must therefore pay real capital and time for every fake identity, and that cost scales linearly while the reward does not.
